findings.title: Date override returns available before checking busy times
findings.body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, once a date override on the slot's date is detected and the slot is considered inside it, the function executes `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` before the `busy.every(...)` check. Any accepted booking or calendar busy time during a date override is therefore ignored for fixed hosts and loose hosts, so a host with a date override can be offered/booked while already busy. The override should only change the working-hours rule; it must still fall through to busy-time validation.

findings.title: Date override window accepts partial overlaps and the end boundary
findings.body: The date-override check only rejects slots that end at/before the override start or start after the override end. It never requires the slot to fit inside the override. A 60-minute event with an override 10:00-11:00 therefore accepts 09:30-10:30 (starts before override) and 11:00-12:00 (starts exactly at override end, because `isAfter` is strict). Those slots are marked available for a fixed host even though they are outside the host's override availability. The condition should require `slotStartTime >= overrideStart` and `slotEndTime <= overrideEnd`.

findings.title: Working-hours end is computed from the slot start
findings.body: The new working-hours check sets `end` to the same value as `start` (`slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`), so `end > workingHour.endTime` can never detect a slot that runs past the host's working-hours end. A fixed host whose working hours end earlier than the aggregate event availability can be offered a slot that starts before their end but finishes after it. `end` should be computed from `slotEndTime`.

findings.title: Multiple date overrides on the same date are treated as one range
findings.body: `dateOverrides.find(...)` returns true and `checkIfIsAvailable` immediately returns false as soon as the slot is outside any override whose date matches. If a user has two overrides on the same date, e.g. 10:00-11:00 and 14:00-15:00, a slot at 14:30 is checked against the first override, found to be after its end, and rejected even though the second override covers it. The code needs to evaluate all overrides for the date and only reject the slot if it is outside every one of them.

findings.title: Active override filter still compares placeholder wall time to invitee day
findings.body: `activeOverrides` filters using `dayjs.utc(override.start)` against the invitee's day, but `override.start` is a wall-clock placeholder stored with UTC fields, not the real UTC instant. For offsets that move the real override onto a different invitee day, the override is dropped or assigned to the wrong day before the new offset calculation runs. Example: organizer Asia/Kolkata override at 14:00 on Jan 2 and invitee timezone +14; the real slot is Jan 2 22:30 invitee time, but raw Jan 2 14:00Z is outside the Jan 2 invitee day, so no override availability is generated for Jan 2. The filter should use the override's actual UTC instant or compare days in the organizer timezone.

findings.title: New test does not cover fixed-host date override filtering
findings.body: The added test only changes the invitee timezone for a personal event. It does not exercise the new fixed-host/round-robin filtering or a date override that conflicts with an existing booking or calendar busy time, so the early-return, partial-overlap, end-boundary, and multiple-override bugs in `checkIfIsAvailable` would not be caught.
